column1: # FLASH-seq run RN26038 -- library metadata.
# Source: the RN26038 LIMS sample sheet (project RN26038, plate eASF_A07136,
# container 27-960439), supplied by the user 2026-07-27. NOTHING in
# data/flashseq/ carries this mapping -- the run directory, the samplesheet.csv
# and the FASTQ filenames all know the libraries only as ZHA8833A1..A10. Without
# this file the run looks like ten comparable samples, which it is not.
# The run is an input-amount titration in duplicate. input_pg is the input
# amount normalised to picograms so it can be used as a numeric x-axis; a
# mammalian cell carries ~10-30 pg of total RNA, so the 30 pg rung is the
# single-cell-equivalent one and is the rung that matters for the VASA-seq
# comparison.
# well is the position on plate eASF_A07136 and is NOT decoration: the human
# CALB1 contamination reported in README.md tracks wells G:1/H:1, not input
# amount, and that is only visible if the well is carried through the analysis.
# qc_verdict is a DECISION, not a measurement, taken by the user 2026-07-27 on
# the evidence in README.md ("The 60 pg pair is contaminated with human CALB1"):
#   ok       usable as it stands
#   caveat   usable if the caveat in qc_note is carried with it
#   exclude  do not use as a data point
# A8 is excluded: 18.3% of it is human CALB1, so it is not a 60 pg measurement
# of anything. That leaves the 60 pg rung with A7 alone and therefore with NO
# replicate, so the 0.8218 in replicate_concordance.tsv is a correlation against
# an excluded library and must not be quoted. The titration conclusion does not
# depend on it: the CLEAN 30 pg pair gives r = 0.8435 independently.
# A8 is still processed and reported everywhere, exactly like the others. The
# verdict is a filter for downstream interpretation, not permission to drop it
# from QC -- its contamination is a finding, and hiding it would lose the well
# effect that identified it.
